issues.legal_issue: A condition attached to withdrawal of a suit for filing a fresh suit applies only when the later suit concerns the same subject matter, assessed by its cause of action and relief claimed.
material_facts: The earlier suit sought recognition of an adoption and partition and separate possession of family property, and was withdrawn with permission to bring a fresh suit subject to payment of the defendants’ costs.
The later suit sought possession of the properties from a trespasser on the basis of title, and was brought before the appellant’s costs in the earlier suit had been paid.
The cause of action in the earlier suit arose from separation from the family, while the later suit rested on transactions forming the basis of title after the deaths of the adoptive parents.
The adoption was relevant in both suits, but the court found it was not the cause of action in either suit.
issues.conclusion: The later suit was not barred by the unpaid-cost condition because it concerned a different subject matter from the earlier suit.
issues.legal_principle: Order 23, Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure permits withdrawal with liberty to bring a fresh suit on terms fixed by the court. “Subject matter” does not mean the property alone; it refers to the right in the property sought to be enforced and includes the cause of action and relief claimed. The subject matter is the series of acts or transactions giving rise to the relief, or the bundle of facts that must be proved to obtain it. Different causes of action and reliefs mean the suits do not concern the same subject matter, and overlap in issues alone does not make their subject matters identical. The court applied Rakhma Bai v. Mahadeo Narayan and approved and applied Singa Reddi v. Subba Reddi.

rule.if: fresh_suit_after_withdrawal and earlier_withdrawal_order_conditions_fresh_suit_on_same_subject_matter and different_causes_of_action and different_relief_claimed

predicates.fresh_suit_after_withdrawal: A plaintiff brings a later suit after withdrawing an earlier suit with permission to bring a fresh one.
predicates.earlier_withdrawal_order_conditions_fres: The court's withdrawal order makes a condition apply to a fresh suit concerning the same subject matter as the earlier suit.
predicates.different_causes_of_action: The facts giving rise to the later claim differ from the facts giving rise to the earlier claim.
predicates.different_relief_claimed: The plaintiff seeks a different form of relief in the later suit from the relief sought in the earlier suit.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff brings a fresh suit after withdrawal and its cause of action and relief differ from those in the earlier suit, the later suit is not barred by an unpaid condition limited to suits on the same subject matter.

issues.legal_issue: Concurrent factual findings on adoption and marital status are not disturbed on appeal without a convincing basis for intervention.
material_facts: The trial court and the High Court both found that the alleged adoption had occurred.
Both courts also found that the person adopted was not married at the time of the adoption.
The Supreme Court found evidence supporting those concurrent findings and no convincing circumstance requiring it to review them.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court declined to disturb the concurrent findings on adoption and marital status.
issues.legal_principle: The court stated that it ordinarily does not interfere with concurrent findings of fact and found no justification to do so in this case. No provision or earlier case was relied on for this ruling.

predicates.appeal_against_concurrent_factual_findin: The matter is an appeal in which the lower courts reached the same findings of fact.
predicates.evidence_supports_findings: The evidence supports the factual findings made by the lower courts.
predicates.no_convincing_basis_to_reopen: No convincing circumstance warrants reopening the concurrent factual findings.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges factual findings shared by the lower courts, evidence supports those findings, and there is no convincing basis to reopen them, the findings are left undisturbed.
